Thanks for the quick response on the intro. We'd like to get a product demo for our APAC engineering and product teams next week. The team spans IST (India) and AEST (Sydney) timezones.

Can you propose two 45-minute slots that would work for both IST and AEST? Rough constraints:
- India (IST) participants are available between 10:00-18:00 IST.
- Sydney (AEST) participants are available between 09:00-17:00 AEST.

Also heads up: several folks will be forwarding the invite internally and some are on calendar clients that previously showed floating/incorrect times when invites crossed zones. Appreciate any guidance to avoid that.

Cheers,

Vanessa,

Thanks — Option A works best for the bulk of the India team. Quick heads up from our side: when Alex sent an earlier invite to a subset of the group last month, some people in Sydney saw the event at a different hour (their clients showed it as a floating time), and when the invite was forwarded internally it sometimes displayed as PST for a few attendees. We've had this happen when an event is created without an explicit tzid or when attendees use older calendar clients.

If you can, please:
- Create the event with Asia/Kolkata as the organizer timezone and explicitly set the event timezone field (not just rely on the organizer's machine timezone).
- Attach an .ics named with the region (e.g., "RDW-demo-APAC-AsiaKolkata.ics") so folks can import directly into Outlook/Apple Calendar if needed.
- Double-check daylight-savings edge cases for any participants that are currently traveling (we have folks moving between AU/NZ this week).

I'm attaching a screenshot of how the forwarded invite appeared on one of our Sydney attendees (shows 11:30 instead of 15:00).

Thanks for handling this — we'll confirm once we see the invite.

Regards,
Priya Nair
Staff Product Manager | Acme Enterprises
Attachment: calendar-screenshot.png
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: RE: Redwood demo request - APAC team availability

Hi Priya / Suresh,

Appreciate the details and the screenshot — that made the issue clear. Apologies for the earlier confusion. Root cause was that the first invite was created without an explicit tzid for the event (Google sometimes stores a floating time if the creator's client uses a local display override). When attendees forwarded the invite, some clients interpreted the floating time in their local zone (hence the PST/incorrect hour).

What I did to fix it:
- Created a new event with explicit timezone set to Asia/Kolkata (for the organizer) and verified the event has the TZ property in the invite.
- Produced a region-specific .ics (calendar-invite-fixed.ics) that you can import into Outlook/Apple clients.
- Also created a separate Australia/Sydney variant so Sydney-based attendees get a native invite in their zone (avoids forwarding issues).
- Re-sent the invite and added a short note in the description with the conversions ("10:30 AM IST / 3:00 PM AEDT").

Final: confirmed slot is Tue, Mar 24 — 10:30 AM IST / 3:00 PM AEDT (45m). I've attached the fixed .ics and re-attached the deck. Please let me know if anyone still sees incorrect times and we'll create a direct calendar share or dial-in-only option.

Thanks — looking forward to the session.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com
Attachments: calendar-invite-fixed.ics, demo-deck-v2.pdf
